subject: Renewal uplift — staged accelerator credits and co-term bridge plan
messages:
From: Jordan Lane <jordan.lane@orbishealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbishealth.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal question — mid-contract add-on and co-term options

Hi Vivek,

We are approaching our renewal window (Dec 1) but our product team expects a mid-quarter spike in inference usage due to a pilot going to production. We need a couple of things clarified before we lock renewals:

- Can we add a 20% capacity uplift mid-contract without re-pricing the full term?
- If we do a mid-contract top-up, can that be co-termed to our Dec 1 renewal date (so invoices align)?
- Are there any short-term credit/discount structures (bridge credits) you offer for staged increases?

Appreciate a short set of options and ballpark economics so I can take to procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan Lane
Head of Platform Engineering
Orbis Health
[Attachment: Orbis-usage-forecast-Q4.xlsx]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lane <jordan.lane@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question — mid-contract add-on and co-term options

Jordan — thanks for the clarity and the forecast. High level options below; I attached a worked example (RWU-Uplift-Scenarios-v2.xlsx). Happy to hop on a 20-min call.

Option A — Top-up as separate add-on (fast, no contract amendment):
- Add-on priced at current committed rate prorated from activation date.
- Billing as a separate line item; renewal stays Dec 1.
- No discount on the top-up; preserves current unit economics.

Option B — Staged uplift with bridge credits (recommended if you want lower unit cost quickly):
- Add the 20% uplift now as a provisional capacity bucket for Q4.
- Apply a one-time bridge credit equal to 25% of the uplift invoice for Q4, recouped over the renewal term if you do not maintain the uplift post-renewal.
- At renewal (Dec 1) we co-term the provisional capacity into the main contract and apply a 6% blended uplift discount on the new committed baseline.

Option C — Immediate re-commit (best for predictable growth):
- Convert to a higher committed tier now; price benefits immediate but requires a contract amendment and sign-off; billing is annualized and co-termed.

Notes:
- Option B gives you most runway to validate usage without full-term commitment.
- We can draft a short amendment (1–2 pages) to add provisional capacity and bridge-credit mechanics; Diego has the pricing matrix.

Next steps: tell us whether you prefer A, B or C and whether procurement needs a formal amendment or a simple PO referencing the HubSpot deal.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lane <jordan.lane@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question — mid-contract add-on and co-term options

Jordan, Vivek — quick operational clarifications from legal/finance: 

1) For Option B: the bridge credit framing we use is a one-time credit applied to the next invoice and documented in a 1pg amendment. If Orbis reduces below the uplifted baseline within 6 months of renewal, a reclaim/prorate applies (we outline reclaim mechanics in the amendment).

2) Co-term mechanics: we can co-term the provisional uplift to your Dec 1 renewal date by issuing a pro-rated credit/invoice to align both contract periods. That requires the amendment to include the new committed baseline and effective date.

3) Procurement paperwork: we can accept a PO referencing DEAL-13792 + sign the short amendment. If you prefer DocuSign, we can send once you confirm option.

Diego — I asked you to run net-new rates for the blended 6% uplift discount referenced by Vivek. Please include both monthly and annualized numbers.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Amendment-Draft-Orbis-2026.pdf]
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lane <jordan.lane@orbishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question — mid-contract add-on and co-term options

Jordan — ran the numbers off your forecast. Key takeaways (see RWU-Uplift-Scenarios-v2.xlsx for line-by-line):

- Current committed baseline: 100k tokens/day equivalent.
- Proposed 20% uplift: +20k tokens/day provisional.
- Option A cost (prorated add-on for Q4): ~$18,300 for the quarter (no discount).
- Option B cost (provisional with 25% bridge credit): billable Q4 cost $13,725 after the one-time credit; if converted at renewal we apply a blended 6% uplift discount across the new baseline which yields ~12% lower per-token cost vs Option A over next year.
- Option C (immediate re-commit): roughly equivalent to Option B over 12 months but requires annualized commit upfront; reduces volatility for Redwood capacity planning.

If Orbis confirms Option B I will prepare the amendment language with reclaim guardrails (6‑month look-back, pro-rata reclaim formula) and produce the DocuSign packet. Jordan — do you want me to push to DocuSign or do you prefer PO-first?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Principal Pricing Analyst | Redwood Inference
